decisions.reason: The keyword-policy change does not alter the source or testimonial-style presentation of the testimonial material.
The source reiterates that the entire script must be in Hindi, but the candidate already requires Hindi only; no state change is necessary.
Requiring additional reference-derived keywords does not change the existing directness or Indian-market alignment of the opening hook.
The creative direction already uses the latest reference as its foundation; the narrower keyword policy does not change that concept-level requirement.
The source changes required keyword diversity but does not change the independently stated requirement for a viral creative style.
The keyword-policy change does not alter the specified audience age range or Indian-market context.
The source does not change the content, placement, or integration of the call to action.
Although keyword choice is motivated by performance concerns, the source does not change the campaign objective, CPL target, or optimization priority.
The script keyword policy has no necessary effect on the unresolved live-action versus AI-generated visual method.
The source does not alter lip-sync accuracy or natural facial-expression requirements.
The keyword-policy change does not alter responsibility for creating the script, visuals, or voiceover.
The source does not change the pilot quantity, duration, aspect ratios, or follow-on order condition.
